mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -45.6% to -36.7%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continues linearly over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the baseline mean of the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days (-41.5%), or reverses by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed (t-0w: -33.0%), signaling persistent commuting avoidance. This sustained transit suppression constrains weekday retail access and foot traffic, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery beyond current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -33.0% in t-0w, only 10.4 points above t-3w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 15 percentage points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -30% while TRANSIT remains below -30%.

This substitution effect reduces pressure on indoor retail venues, capping RETAIL_REC gains to less than 5 percentage points over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stabilizes within ±2% of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 15.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days while PARKS remains near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility shows consistent improvement (from -21.7% to -11.3%), indicating normalized essential shopping patterns. This normalization of essential mobility signals broader confidence in public spaces, triggering discretionary retail visits and lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 10.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 3 percentage points in any week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 3 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains severely depressed (t-0w: -44.3%), indicating continued remote work or capacity restrictions. If WORKPLACES does not recover above -35% within two weeks, office-adjacent retail (lunch, after-work shopping) remains suppressed, preventing RETAIL_REC from exceeding -30% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -35% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves by more than 10 percentage points in a single week, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -25% while WORKPLACES remains below -35%.

This sustained decline in residential confinement, combined with RETAIL_REC's upward trend, signals seasonal reopening momentum that accelerates RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 0.5 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.3 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL increases above 10% in any week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 4 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of TRANSIT (-33.0%), WORKPLACES (-44.3%), and RETAIL_REC (-36.7%) suppression indicates a coordinated mobility collapse. Recovery requires simultaneous improvement across all three series. If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not both improve by at least 8 percentage points within one week, RETAIL_REC remains trapped below -35% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by less than 8 percentage points in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds -30% over the next 28 days while either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES remains below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovery (10.4 point improvement) combined with PARKS stabilization (0.7% at baseline) indicates consumer confidence in public spaces is returning. This confidence threshold, once crossed, triggers discretionary retail spending. If both conditions hold for two weeks, RETAIL_REC accelerates by at least 6 percentage points over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 3 percentage points AND PARKS remains within ±1% of baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by less than 4 percentage points over the next 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 2 percentage points in any week.
